recognize_zh: 心包液抹片中幾乎滿視野都是分葉核的嗜中性球，僅夾雜少數較大、核圓的巨噬細胞或間皮細胞，背景有少量紅血球，屬急性化膿性（neutrophil-predominant）滲出液。
features: Markedly cellular fluid composed predominantly of segmented neutrophils
Neutrophils with 2–4 nuclear lobes and pale pink cytoplasm; some degenerative changes
Scattered larger mononuclear cells (macrophages/mesothelial cells) with round nuclei and gray-blue cytoplasm
Background of scattered red blood cells and proteinaceous material
No malignant cell clusters or organisms identifiable at this magnification
describe_en: Cytocentrifuge preparation of pericardial fluid shows a markedly cellular specimen composed predominantly of segmented neutrophils. Scattered macrophages and occasional mesothelial-type cells are present in a background of red blood cells and proteinaceous debris. No atypical cell clusters are seen, and organisms cannot be assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with a neutrophil-predominant (acute inflammatory/purulent) pericardial effusion; correlation with Gram stain and culture is recommended.

ddx.vs: Tuberculous and viral effusions are dominated by small mature lymphocytes rather than sheets of segmented neutrophils.
Malignant effusions contain cohesive three-dimensional clusters of atypical cells with nuclear pleomorphism, which are absent here.
Blood contamination yields a white cell differential mirroring blood with abundant RBCs, not a dense near-pure neutrophil population.
